Riding the NC500: The Right Bike Matters

The North Coast 500 is Britain's most famous motorcycle route — 516 miles of stunning Scottish coastline, mountain passes, and single-track roads. The route's varied terrain makes bike choice particularly important. From sweeping dual carriageways to narrow single-track roads with passing places, the NC500 demands a versatile, manageable machine.

NC500 Road Conditions

The route includes everything from smooth A-roads to rough single-track with potholes, gravel patches, and livestock wandering across the tarmac. The western section between Applecross and Durness features tight, twisty single-track roads where a heavy bike becomes a liability. Wind exposure on coastal sections can be extreme. Rain is almost guaranteed at some point during any NC500 attempt.

Best Bikes for the NC500

Yamaha Tenere 700 — Arguably the perfect NC500 bike. Light enough for single-track roads, tough enough for rough surfaces, and comfortable enough for the longer A-road sections. The manageable 204kg weight makes it confidence-inspiring when the road narrows to one lane.

Triumph Tiger 900 Rally — The triple engine loves the NC500's twisty sections. Light enough for single-track and powerful enough for A9 dual carriageway blasts. Wire wheels handle rough surfaces with confidence.

BMW R 1300 GS — The GS handles the NC500 beautifully despite its size. Electronic suspension adapts to surface changes, and the boxer engine's torque makes single-track riding relaxed. However, its width can be challenging on the narrowest sections.

Honda CB500X — For budget-conscious riders, the CB500X handles the NC500 admirably. Light and manageable on single-track, economical, and reliable. The only limitation is motorway comfort for the long ride up to Inverness.

Suzuki V-Strom 650 — Another excellent budget choice with a more powerful engine than the Honda. The V-twin provides relaxed cruising and the chassis handles the NC500's varied surfaces well.

Essential Setup for the NC500

  • Tyres — Fresh touring tyres with at least 80 percent tread. The NC500's varied surfaces demand good grip in all conditions.
  • Screen — A taller screen for the exposed coastal sections where crosswinds and rain are constant companions.
  • Luggage — Keep it minimal. Heavy luggage transforms manageable single-track into a white-knuckle experience.
  • Rain gear — Guaranteed to need it. Pack top-quality waterproofs accessible without unpacking everything.
Ride the NC500 anticlockwise. The scenery builds to a climax along the dramatic west coast, and you tackle the challenging single-track sections fresh at the start of each day rather than tired at the end.

faq.q: What is the best bike for the NC500?
faq.a: The Yamaha Tenere 700 is arguably perfect: light enough for single-track roads, tough enough for rough surfaces and comfortable enough for the longer A-road sections. Its manageable 204kg weight is confidence-inspiring when the road narrows to one lane with passing places.

faq.q: Can I ride the NC500 on a budget bike?
faq.a: Yes. The Honda CB500X handles the NC500 admirably, being light, manageable on single-track, economical and reliable, with the main limitation being motorway comfort on the run up to Inverness. The Suzuki V-Strom 650 is another strong budget choice with a more powerful engine.

faq.q: How should I set up my bike for the route?
faq.a: Fit fresh touring tyres with at least 80 percent tread, add a taller screen for exposed coastal crosswinds, and keep luggage minimal as heavy loads make single-track a white-knuckle experience. Pack top-quality waterproofs somewhere accessible without unpacking everything.

faq.q: Should I ride clockwise or anticlockwise?
faq.a: Ride the NC500 anticlockwise. The scenery builds to a climax along the dramatic west coast, and you tackle the challenging single-track sections fresh at the start of each day rather than tired at the end, which makes the tightest stretches far safer and more enjoyable.
